cmad.notes: Two revisions were located and both were used. The current CMAD (v2.1, released 2024-09-01 for the 2023 Heliophysics Senior Review, DOI 10.48322/vshd-sv21, registered in SPASE as spase://NASA/Document/MMS/CMAD) carries a 40-name author list; that list opens with Burch and Giles and is alphabetized from the third name onward, so being named on it is the evidence, not position within it. Revision 0 (prepared 2020-05-06 by Kristopher Larsen, downloadable from the LASP MMS Science Working Team space) carries a signature page naming the mission PI, project scientist, program scientist, project manager, Science Operations Center leads, and the lead of each instrument suite - the single richest role-labelled source found in this run. Both post-date the 2015 start of operations, so both describe operating-era teams; where they differ, v2.1 is the more recent statement. A CMAD was expected: MMS is an operational, NASA-funded mission still under senior review.

instrument_coverage.notes: The MMS Observatory record has no downward instrument links, so the SPASE side was established by reverse lookup of https://spase-metadata.org/SMWG/Instrument/MMS/ and confirmed against a local clone of the SMWG repository. Fifty-two Instrument records exist: the thirteen listed above, replicated identically under MMS/1, MMS/2, MMS/3 and MMS/4. Note that each of those records sets ObservatoryID to spase://SMWG/Observatory/MMS/<n>, the per-spacecraft Observatory records, which in turn set ObservatoryGroupID to spase://SMWG/Observatory/MMS - so no Instrument record points directly at the record being processed, and a naive ObservatoryID match would have found none. The external roster was taken from the MMS Science Data Center dataset index, the mission instruments page, the mission overview paper and the CMAD chapter structure; all four agree. Every instrument on the roster has a SPASE record, so nothing is missing. Two mapping details: SPASE folds the analogue (AFG, UCLA) and digital (DFG, IWF Graz) fluxgate magnetometers into one FGM record, and the SDC's 'Ephemerides' products correspond to the SPASE Ephemeris record and the CMAD's Magnetic Ephemeris Coordinates (MEC) chapter. SPASE additionally carries a DSP record that the SDC dataset index does not break out separately.

pending_instrument_runs.notes: No peer-reviewed description paper exists for the MMS ephemeris products; they are documented only in chapter 3 of the CMAD, which names no MEC lead. The Instrument record's Contacts list only James L. Burch as mission PrincipalInvestigator, so no instrument-specific person was recoverable. A dedicated run should pursue the MEC software authors through the MMS Science Data Center and the SPEDAS MEC documentation.

pending_instrument_runs.reason: author-order classification limits what the paper yields
pending_instrument_runs.notes: The description paper (Russell et al. 2016, 10.1007/s11214-014-0057-3) was confidently identified, but its author list is alphabetized from the second author to the nineteenth, leaving Russell as the only author whose position carries contribution information. Anderson and Baumjohann, who follow him, are recorded as excluded for that reason. A dedicated FGM run should establish the AFG and DFG sub-instrument leads from UCLA and IWF Graz provider pages, since the paper cannot supply them.

notes: The MMS Observatory record is minimal: a Description, one Contact (James L. Burch as PrincipalInvestigator), two InformationURLs, and no OperatingSpan element at all. The operating span reported here (2015-03-13, still open) was taken from the OperatingSpan of the MMS Instrument records, all of which give StartDate 2015-03-13T02:44:00 with no StopDate. The missing OperatingSpan on the Observatory record itself is worth flagging to curators.

Paper selection was confident for the mission overview and for every instrument paper used. All are from the 2016 Space Science Reviews MMS special issue (volume 199), published within a year of the 2015 start of operations; each names its instrument in the title, carries a large team author list, and is heavily cited (the mission overview at over 1200 citations, the FPI paper over 1000, the magnetometers paper over 900). Crossref, the CMAD reference lists and the MMS Science Data Center all point to the same set, so no downgrade was applied.

Author-order classification, paper by paper. Mission overview (Burch et al. 2016, n=4): backward scan finds a sorted suffix of 1, so not alphabetized; authors 1-3 (Burch, Moore, Torbert) are Strong and author 4 (Giles) is Medium, this being the record's own description paper. FIELDS suite (n=34), SCM (n=30), ADP/DSP (n=20), SDP (n=21), EDI (n=24): sorted suffixes of 1 and longest internal sorted runs of 3-4, all below the five-name threshold, so all four are treated as not alphabetized and positions 1-3 taken. FPI (n=97): sorted suffix of 32 from author 66, with further sorted blocks at 8-16 and 17-65, so partially alphabetized with a deliberate prefix; positions 1-3 (Pollock, Moore, Jacques) taken. HPCA (n=29): sorted suffix of 15 from author 15, prefix 1-14, positions 1-3 taken. EIS (n=26): sorted suffix of 18 from author 9, prefix 1-8, positions 1-3 taken. FEEPS (n=27): sorted suffix of 25 from author 3, so the prefix is only two names - Blake and Mauk were taken and nothing was padded from the alphabetized tail. ASPOC (n=9): sorted suffix of 2, not alphabetized, positions 1-3 taken.

The MMS magnetometers paper (Russell et al. 2016) is the one case where the backward-scan rule and the evidence disagree. The scan finds a sorted suffix of only 1, because four names (Hagen, Jernej, Valavanoglou, Richter) were appended after the main list - but authors 2 through 19 form an unbroken alphabetical run of eighteen, which cannot be coincidence. The list was therefore read as a one-name prefix (Russell) followed by an alphabetized block and a short appendix. Only Russell earns position-based evidence; Anderson and Baumjohann, who sit at the head of the alphabetized block, are recorded as excluded. Baumjohann in particular is a senior figure in the MMS magnetometer effort, so a reviewer may wish to reinstate him - but no source found in this run (CMAD, Contacts, provider pages) corroborates him, and the rule is applied symmetrically rather than case by case.

This being an Observatory record, each instrument contributed its leads only: every qualifying-role person in the Instrument record Contacts, plus positions 1-3 of the instrument's description paper. Authors at position 4 and beyond in an instrument paper are instrument-team depth and belong to that Instrument record's own run; they were not enumerated individually here, since the eleven instrument papers carry over 300 authors between them. Several of those deeper authors are nevertheless included candidates, but every one of them earned it through an independent source - the CMAD author list, an Instrument record contact role, or the mission overview paper - and not through their instrument-paper position.

The FIELDS suite paper was treated as a suite-level description alongside the six individual FIELDS instrument papers, because FIELDS is a distinct grouping in SPASE (seven Instrument records sit under MMS/n/FIELDS/) and the CMAD and mission pages treat it as one investigation with a single named lead. Positions 1-3 were taken from the suite paper (Torbert, Russell, Magnes) and from each member instrument's own paper. The same reasoning applies to the EPD suite, whose EIS paper (Mauk et al. 2016) is explicitly both the suite and the EIS description, and to FPI, whose single paper covers both DES and DIS.

Instrument PIs and suite leads are recorded as InstrumentLead with the instrument named, never as PrincipalInvestigator; that role is reserved here for James L. Burch, the PI of the mission as a whole. InstrumentLead was assigned only where a source explicitly names the person as lead or PI of that instrument - the CMAD signature page or an Instrument record Description - and not merely because they led its description paper. So Torbert (FIELDS), Gershman and Giles (FPI), Cohen (EPD), Torkar and Nakamura (ASPOC), Fuselier (HPCA), Mauk (EIS/EPD), Blake (FEEPS) and Russell (FGM) carry the role, while Ergun, Le Contel, Lindqvist, Pollock and Young, who lead papers but are not named lead anywhere in the sources fetched, carry Author alone.

James L. Burch is listed as PrincipalInvestigator in the Contacts of all fifty-two MMS Instrument records. That is mission-level evidence repeated at instrument level, not fifty-two instrument PI-ships, and it is recorded once as a mission PrincipalInvestigator role.

Christopher T. Russell appears in the FGM Instrument record Contacts with role TeamLeader, which is not author-qualifying. He is an included candidate on other grounds entirely - lead author of the magnetometers paper, second author of the FIELDS suite paper, and a CMAD author - and his TeamLeader entry is recorded as context only.

Three names from the 2020 CMAD signature page do not appear in the 2024 v2.1 author list: Galen Fowler (NASA MMS Program Scientist), Kristopher Larsen (who prepared Revision 0) and Chris Pankratz (Science Operations Center Lead). All three are included on the strength of the 2020 document, with the era noted; a reviewer checking against the current team should expect them to be earlier-generation. James Clapsadle, the fourth such name, is excluded because his stated function is project management.

The MMS Calibration and Measurement Algorithms Document v2.1 author string in the SPASE Document record contains a transcription error - "Eichelberger, Hans UlrichLe, Guan" is missing a separator - and the same list carries a separate seventeenth name, "Hans, Ulrich". These are almost certainly the same person, Hans Ulrich Eichelberger of IWF Graz. Eichelberger is included; "Ulrich Hans" is recorded as excluded, flagged as the artifact. A curator should verify this against the CMAD PDF before publication.

The MMS interdisciplinary-science team page names three IDS team leads (Melvyn L. Goldstein, Martin V. Goldman, Tai Phan). Being named on a provider team page is normally Medium evidence, but IDS teams analyse MMS data rather than build or operate the observatory, none of the three appears in the CMAD author list or the mission overview paper, and TeamLeader is not an author-qualifying role - so all three are recorded as excluded rather than included. This is a judgment call a reviewer may want to revisit.

Two further observatory-scope papers were consulted but produced no candidates on their own: the operations and data system paper (Baker et al. 2016, 10.1007/s11214-014-0128-5) and the mission profile and operations paper (Fuselier et al. 2016, 10.1007/s11214-014-0087-x). Neither is the mission description paper, so no position-based evidence was drawn from them; they appear in information_urls and were used only to corroborate Baker, Fuselier and Pankratz, all of whom are included through other sources.

Person records exist in the SMWG registry for all but three included candidates: Galen Fowler and Christopher K. Pankratz have none, and several instrument-paper leads are registered only under initials (P.Leroy, S.Tucker, J.Westfall, G.Olsson, M.Granoff, A.Jacques, M.Tajmar). Downstream work should expand those initials to full names and confirm identity before creating or citing the records.

ORCIDs were almost entirely absent from Crossref for the 2016 Space Science Reviews papers; only Craig J. Pollock's was registered. Affiliations shown here come from the CMAD signature page, the SPASE Instrument record Descriptions and the papers' own institutional attributions, and should be treated as era-specific rather than current.
